property_summary: The rate() function is value-stable when called a second time at the same block timestamp, because the elapsed time is zero and the accumulated multiplier/index are not modified again.

Calling rate(vault, asset) a second time at the same block timestamp returns exactly the same value as the first call, because no time has elapsed and the stored index/multiplier are not updated twice.
Calling rate(vault, asset) twice at the same block timestamp returns exactly the same value both times when the slope kink has been configured.
Calling rate(vault, asset) twice in the same block timestamp returns the same value both times, provided the slope kink is configured and the test's access-control calls succeed.
Calling rate(vault, asset) twice at the same block timestamp returns the same value both times, provided the slope kink is configured and the test's access-control calls succeed.
For any asset, setSlopes accepts a nonzero kink below 1e27 and emits SetSlopes with exactly the submitted slope values.
For any asset and any nonzero kink strictly less than 1e27, calling setSlopes with arbitrary slope0 and slope1 does not revert.
For any asset and any nonzero kink strictly less than 1e27, calling setSlopes with arbitrary slope0 and slope1 does not revert.
For any asset and any nonzero kink strictly less than 1e27, calling setSlopes with arbitrary slope0 and slope1 never reverts.

For any asset, kink in (0, 1e27), and slope values, setSlopes(asset, (kink, slope0, slope1)) never reverts when called by an authorized caller (the test contract is the deployed contract's initializer/access-control).

rate(_vault,_asset) never reverts for arbitrary vaults and assets because it only calls IVault view methods and computes from uncapped arithmetic, and the storage fields it mutates (per-vault utilization data) cannot be observed or cause a revert.
setSlopes reverts exactly when the proposed kink is zero or at least 1e27, provided the caller is authorized by the access control contract.
For any asset address and any non-zero kink strictly below 1e27, when the caller is authorized by the access control contract, setSlopes succeeds and never reverts.
For any asset and any valid non-zero kink below 1e27, calling setSlopes as the authorized caller never reverts; the call simply stores the slopes and emits SetSlopes.
setSlopes with a valid kink succeeds and does not revert.
For any asset address and any kink strictly between 0 and 1e27, when the caller is authorized by the access control contract, setSlopes does not revert.
setSlopes always succeeds when the given kink is in (0, 1e27), and after such a call the asset's slope data is exactly the supplied values.
For any asset and any valid kink strictly between 0 and 1e27, a direct call to setSlopes by the test contract never reverts.
For any asset and any valid kink strictly between 0 and 1e27, a call to setSlopes succeeds and the stored slope data equals the supplied values.
For any asset and any valid kink strictly between 0 and 1e27, a direct call to setSlopes by the test contract never reverts.
For any asset and any kink in (0, 1e27), calling setSlopes succeeds and the stored kink equals the provided kink.
A successful setLimits call with any inputs either reverts with AccessDenied or leaves maxMultiplier/minMultiplier getters reading exactly the passed values.

property_summary: Calling setSlopes with any valid kink in (0, 1e27) followed by setLimits(1e27, 1e27, 0) makes rate(_vault, _asset) return exactly 0 for any vault/asset, because the rate multiplier is set to 0 and the interest rate is a non-negative value multiplied by that zero multiplier.
